reviewed_interfaces_changed.warning: M01's specified interfaces conflicted with contracts B00 froze and merged. All changes are ADDITIVE and B00's suite passes unchanged, but they touch shared files outside M01's allowed paths and REQUIRE REVIEW.
changes: AccessPort gained authorize()->Decision and require_recent_2fa(); check()/is_allowed() now derive from authorize().

ModuleRegistration: permission codes may be multi-segment; ownership declared as permission_prefixes (default '<slug>.'); added api_path_roots, middleware, public_paths and assert_no_registration_collisions().
RelationshipFacts gained school_id, section_ids, subject_ids, valid_until and is_active_on().
EventEnvelope gained correlation_id and schema_version (envelope_version retained one revision; retire in v4).
RegistryPort gained get_student, get_roster, get_relationships, get_teaching_assignments; the shared fake implements all four.
ErrorCode gained RATE_LIMITED -> 429 with a finite Retry-After.
New contract types: contracts/decisions.py (Decision, ReasonCode), contracts/people.py (Registry DTOs).
Shared middleware yields to a module-resolved context, AFTER running the spoofed-header and body guards for every request.
The port registry moved from settings.SCHOOL_PORTS to a process-level holder.
config/urls.py reads DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE instead of settings.SETTINGS_MODULE.
PlatformPort was NOT changed; M01 uses an internal facade.

defects_found.detail: doctor gates on .venv existing and correctly exited 2 on a bare runner, failing the job before it installed anything. doctor behaved as designed; the workflow step order was wrong.
defects_found.fix: doctor now runs twice: non-gating diagnostics first, then gating after the install.

defects_found.defect: The requires_postgres race test could never run
defects_found.detail: It called pytest.skip() unconditionally, so the marker promised concurrency coverage that NO environment could deliver -- including the PostgreSQL job, where it still reported skipped.
defects_found.fix: Implemented as a real two-connection race with a threading.Barrier so both threads attempt the conditional UPDATE simultaneously. The skip is now decided from the live connection vendor.

ci_first_run.useful_finding: The GitHub runner reports 'container engine running (server 28.0.4)', so the browser suite genuinely can run in CI once the ordering is fixed.

results.M01 access suite on real PostgreSQL: success (159 passed, 0 skipped -- the real race ran)

defect_found.defect: Generated Compose files used the wrong relative path depth
defect_found.detail: Compose resolves build contexts and bind mounts against the directory CONTAINING the compose file, not the invocation directory. The generated file lives at dev/state/<stem>.compose.yaml, two levels below the root, but the context was '..' -- so infra/backend.Dockerfile resolved to dev/infra/backend.Dockerfile and Compose failed with 'lstat .../dev/infra: no such file or directory'.
defect_found.why_it_survived_this_long: YAML validation, digest pinning and service-selection tests all passed on this file. Only actually building could find it, and nothing had ever built it: this was the first execution of the Compose path anywhere.
defect_found.fix: A single REPO_ROOT_FROM_COMPOSE constant derived from the file's real depth, applied to the context and all three bind mounts. A regression test resolves every generated path for every module and asserts it exists; it was confirmed to FAIL with the old value.

defect_found.defect: Both container images copied source as root while running as an unprivileged user
defect_found.detail: Vite writes a temporary bundle of its config NEXT TO vite.config.ts when loading it (vite.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs). /app/frontend was root-owned from the COPY, so the dev server died immediately with EACCES.
defect_found.progress: The images BUILT and the containers STARTED -- two steps further than the previous attempt. The build-context fix worked.
defect_found.fix: Both Dockerfiles now chown their tree to the runtime user and COPY --chown. Running as root would also 'fix' it, and would create root-owned files in the developer's checkout through the bind mount, so ownership is the correct fix rather than dropping the unprivileged user.
defect_found.not_verifiable_locally: There is no container engine on the development machine, so CI is the only place this can be confirmed.
